meta.notes: 9-week post-White River rebuild to Vermont 50K (Sun 9/27: 32-33 mi, ~5,600 ft as 20+ repeated climbs/descents, 37% gravel road, NO POLES). PHASES: W1-2 recovery-dominant (walk/run rebuild, symptom-gated), W3-6 Build, W7 Peak, W8 Taper, W9 Race week. WEEKLY SKELETON (W3+): Mon rest / Tue hill intervals + PM Lower A / Wed easy + upper / Thu easy w-descent block + PM Lower B / Fri easy + strides or gear-change pickups / Sat shakeout + upper / SUN LONG RUN (moved to Sunday to match race day). Run before strength on every double day; no lower-body strength day-of or day-before the long run. PRIORITY MAP: P1 tendon durability lives in the strength plan and daily routines; P2 hill intervals (pole-free, absorbs runnable-grade economy) from W3; P3 descent capacity gated — Gate 1 (PT assessment) CLEARED pre-plan, gentle exposure from W3, Gate 2 descent-calibration session W5 Thursday clears race-specific volume from W6. INTENSITY DECISION (coach-owned, re-derived rev 1.4): hill intervals Z3-capped per the validated HR-led model; plus short 15-20s uphill strides from W3 — alactic, low-eccentric. STRIDE RATIONALE RE-DERIVED: the original justification cited the +4..8% cadence-collapse finding, RETRACTED 8/6/2026 (Findings Register F-02) — running cadence is 166-178 spm at every grade on all three reference files. Strides are retained on independent grounds: running economy, and the SSC/elastic-tendon demand of Vermont's 20-28 short climb-descent transitions. Strides remain the first thing pulled on any lateral-ankle symptom. No sustained Z4+ work this cycle. GRADE POLICY (new rev 1.4, band-differentiated — replaces the blanket run-everything cue): BELOW +5% run everything, standing instruction, this is where the prize is densest because running's advantage over hiking shrinks as grade rises. +5..8% is a DECLARED TEST ZONE, not an assumed deficit — F-08 is open and the W4 Tuesday test resolves it. ABOVE +8% hike deliberately; Vermont holds only ~5% of its distance above +10%. CADENCE CRITERION (corrected rev 1.4): all climb-rep pass/fail is on run_pct >= 80%, NEVER on a cadence number. Prior cues of 'cadence 130+' and 'cadence 140+' were blend-level figures inherited from walk-contaminated band averages and would pass a half-walked rep. Report cadence_moving_spm alongside. Descent cues moved to median running cadence 175+ to match the analyzer thresholds. TARGET FRAMING (rev 1.4): the training target is ABSOLUTE PACE AT A SUSTAINABLE HR. GAP-parity at grade is NOT a goal and must not be gated on — every climb band on all three reference files already sits at or below a GAP/flat ratio of 1.00 while power hiking, because Minetti is a running model applied outside its domain (Addendum B v4 C-7, Findings Register F-07). FLAT ANCHOR: sustained-block flat running is 10:39-11:00 at peak fitness and 11:18-11:31 detrained. Band averages (11:32 / 13:03) understate the engine and must not be used as targets. LOAD-PATTERN GUARD (June injury lesson): long runs on ROLLING RUNNABLE terrain (100-150 ft/mi, gravel/dirt ideal), never technical-descent mountain routes; min 6 days between long runs; RAMP GUARD (rev 1.2 — rewritten per Race_Strategy_Response_v1 Answers A1/A2/A3). DENOMINATOR: the guard is enforced against SUMMED SESSIONS, never against weekly_targets. weekly_targets.mileage_mi and .vertical_ft are DERIVED fields regenerated from each week's own session sums; they must never be hand-authored, and any loader should assert equality within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. Rationale: the guard protects tissue, and tissue experiences what is prescribed, not what is summarized. RULES: (1) the W2->W3 step is the recovery-exit rebuild and is exempt from BOTH the percentage and the absolute caps — on session sums it is +9.5 mi / +2,150 ft (14.5 -> 24.0 mi, 300 -> 2,450 ft), roughly double what the old header view (12 -> 19 mi) implied, and it REQUIRES EXPLICIT COACH SIGN-OFF before Week 3 begins; it is not approved by default. (2) absolute caps of +5 mi AND +500 ft apply to any ramp BEGINNING from a week whose session-summed mileage is <=30 mi — the STARTING week is the test. (3) once the starting week exceeds 30 mi the cap is 10%, applied SEPARATELY to mileage and to vertical, each against its own prior-week session sum. (4) any breach pauses the progression at the prior week's volume and flags the coach. COMPLIANCE AT REV 1.2, all on session sums: W3->W4 +5.0 mi / +500 ft (at cap, compliant); W4->W5 +5.0 mi / +500 ft (at cap, compliant); W5->W6 +8.8% mi / +8.7% ft (compliant); W6->W7 +8.1% mi / +9.3% ft (compliant); W7->W8 and W8->W9 both decrease. No breaches. HEADROOM WARNING: the vertical ladder now runs at 87-100% of its ceiling in every build week, and W4 and W5 sit EXACTLY at +500 ft. There is no spare vertical anywhere in W4-W7. Adding gain to any session — including route substitutions that happen to climb more — breaks compliance downstream. The B1 rehearsal spec consumed the last of the headroom; any further vertical request must be funded by an explicit trim elsewhere, not absorbed. W2->W3 EXEMPTION — SETTLED RULE (Run_Plan_rev1_2_Verification_Memo section 3, no longer provisional): the exemption covers BOTH the percentage and the absolute caps. Rationale: the ramp guard is a build-phase instrument, and W2 is a symptom-gated walk/run rebuild whose session sums are not load-comparable to run weeks — walk miles are not run miles — so no arithmetic rule spanning W2->W3 is meaningful in either direction. Governance of that step belongs to the three symptom gates plus the conditional sign-off below, not to the ladder. No re-solve is triggered by this ruling. W2->W3 CONDITIONAL SIGN-OFF (athlete-set, closes the last open human item): the step is PRE-APPROVED AT FULL SIZE (+9.5 mi / +2,150 ft on session sums, 14.5 -> 24.0 mi and 300 -> 2,450 ft) IF AND ONLY IF Weeks 1 and 2 clear all three symptom gates — right lateral ankle, left outer knee, right forefoot — with NO flags. Clean gates means Week 3 starts as written, no further approval needed. ANY flag in W1 or W2 voids the pre-approval, and the ladder re-solves downward with the B1 rehearsal reverting to its 2,600 ft profile (the coupling is stated in the rev 1.2 cover note section 5). Note that a flag severe enough to trigger the existing W1-W2 reset rule is governed by that rule first — reset to the Week 1 Friday level and message the coach — and only then does the reduced-ladder branch apply to whatever Week 3 becomes. LADDER SLACK, computed so the re-solve is not improvised under symptom pressure: holding the 40.0 mi peak week, the W3 floor is 23.06 mi. Against the prescribed 24.0 that is only 0.94 mi of slack — the MILEAGE ladder is effectively rigid, and any meaningful reduction at W3 pulls the peak week down proportionally rather than being absorbed. Vertical is different: the W3 floor is 2,388 ft with the B1 spec intact (62 ft of slack) but 2,058 ft once the rehearsal reverts to 2,600 (392 ft of slack). So the reverted branch buys vertical room and almost no mileage room. Anyone re-solving this ladder should size W3 first, then let W4-W7 fall out of the caps, and expect the peak week to shrink with it; any two of (long run, descent session, steep hill session) never on consecutive days. RECALIBRATION CHECKPOINT W5: Thursday Gate 2 descent session + Sunday rolling calibration long run, both recorded clean and FIT files sent to the Race Strategy project for the Vermont pacing plan v1. Addendum A June-13 tables are CEILINGS from peak fitness — context only, not current targets; the W5 calibration supersedes them. HR ZONES at LTHR 168 — CORRECTED CONTIGUOUS TABLE (per HR_Zone_Gap_Report_v1; orphan bpm values 150/158/167 assigned to their nearest percentage boundary): Z1 Recovery <142 | Z2 Aerobic 142-150 | Z3 Tempo 151-158 | Z4 Sub-threshold 159-167 | Z5a Threshold 168-171. Z5b/c undefined by design — nothing in this program operates there. Nothing operational moves: first-10-mi cap 149 (inside Z2), descent throttle 152 (low Z3), never-cross 158 (now cleanly top of Z3). FIELD CONVENTION: hr_zone = INTENDED EXECUTION BAND (range labels like Z1-2/Z2-3 allowed where intent spans a boundary); hr_cap_bpm = HARD CEILING / alarm value, which may sit above the intended band as a declared tripwire. DOWNSTREAM: whoever parses the Week-5 calibration FIT files (8/27 Gate 2 + 8/30 long run) must bucket HR with these same zone edges (150 in Z2, 158 in Z3) — flag in the parser workflow before processing, not after. SYMPTOM GATES throughout: right lateral-ankle tendon (unproven under load), left outer knee, right forefoot — any recurrence pauses descent work and strides, flags the coach. WEEKLY VERTICAL COMPLIANCE CHECK (added rev 1.3 per verification memo section 4): the Sunday compliance check is extended beyond session completion. Each Sunday, compare ACTUAL GPS-measured weekly vertical against that week's derived weekly_targets.vertical_ft. Because the vertical ladder runs at 87-100% of its ceiling in every build week (W4 and W5 sit exactly at +500 ft), a route substitution that climbs 200 ft over plan is a guard breach, not a rounding difference — the check must catch it the week it happens, not at the next review. Over by more than ~100 ft: the following week's ceiling recomputes off the ACTUAL sum, not the plan, and the coach is messaged. This applies with full force to the two calibration days (8/27 Gate 2 and 8/30 long run), where planned-vs-actual is also checked on the Race Strategy side when the FIT files arrive.
meta.revision_notes: RECONCILED 1.5 (2026-08-09): rev 1.5 was authored against a base predating rev 1.4a-1.4e, so as delivered it reverted the 8/18 terrain field to trail, duration to 50 min, and dropped the locked course, plus the 8/11 non-technical terrain note. Those are RESTORED here and rev 1.5's three edits are grafted on top; 8/18 block names in the decay read-out are remapped to the locked course (A/C = +5.0%, B = +8.5%). With that done the rev 1.5 claim below holds: no distance, duration, vertical or HR cap differs from rev 1.4e. || CURRENT REVISION 1.5 (2026-08-09). THREE key_cue/notes edits only — NO schema change, no new fields, no new session types, no change to any distance, duration, vertical or HR cap. (1) 8/16 gait rule: hikes held >=60 continuous seconds. (2) 8/18 walked recoveries onto the card, plus the BLOCK 2 vs BLOCK 4 decay control in the read-out. (3) 9/13 S6 pole-free hiking block, substituting for running, not added to it. Optional 8/18 closing flat block REFUSED. 8/25 UNCHANGED. Source: Strategist_Dispositions_20260809_v2 s3/s4/s6/s7. NOTE: meta.schema_version remains "1.4" and this is INTENTIONAL — the schema did not change in rev 1.5, only key_cue and notes text on three existing sessions. schema_version and revision are independent fields; do not read the former as the plan revision. || PRIOR REVISIONS, newest first: rev 1.4 (2026-08-06): implements the Addendum C review and the June 13 / May 30 re-parse. (1) FINDING RETRACTED: Addendum A s1c Finding 1 (cadence collapse at +5%) is an artifact of raw band-average cadence measuring walk share. Confirmed on all three reference files — running cadence is 166-178 spm at every grade including above +18%. June 13 run_pct was 38.9% at +2..5%, 3.8% at +5..10%, 0.3% above +10%. (2) CADENCE CRITERION CORRECTED across every quality session: climb-rep pass/fail moves from cadence numbers (130-140 spm, blend level) to run_pct >= 80%. This was the single most consequential defect — a rep held at 135 spm is roughly half walking and passed as written. Descent cues moved 170+ -> median 175+ to match the analyzer thresholds; descent findings themselves are UNAFFECTED by the retraction (descent bands ran 76-92%). (3) STRIDE AND PICKUP RATIONALES RE-DERIVED on economy and SSC grounds; the W4 Friday citation of '13:31 / cadence 138' replaced with the decomposed figures. (4) NEW SESSION: W4 Tuesday 8/18 becomes the F-08 grade-economy test (Addendum C s9) — road or graded fireroad, lap-pressed blocks, flat reference plus +3..4% and +6..7% sustained blocks, run to completion with 157 as an abort tripwire rather than a pacing target. VERTICAL-NEUTRAL: 800 ft unchanged, blocks funded from approach and recovery climbing. Heat gate: slips to W5 Tuesday 8/25 if heat index exceeds 85 F. Must precede the 8/27 Gate 2 and 8/30 calibration package. (5) GRADE POLICY band-differentiated: run everything below +5%, +5..8% is a declared test zone, hike above +8%. (6) TARGET FRAMING: absolute pace at a sustainable HR. GAP-parity explicitly rejected as a goal or gate. NO LOAD CHANGES: every session's distance_mi, elevation_gain_ft and duration_min are identical to rev 1.3. The ladder, ramp-guard compliance and the B1 rehearsal spec are unchanged. Gate 2 pass criteria remain the process criteria (cadence and 24h symptom response); Addendum C s8's GAP-ratio proposal is DECLINED as a gate and retained as a reported metric only, per Addendum B s9 caveat 4. Strength and nutrition plans UNCHANGED. Companion documents: Analysis_Addendum_B_v4.txt, Findings_Register_v1.txt, post_run_analyzer_v2.md.

exercises.name: Walking knee hugs
exercises.cue: Pull knee to chest, balance on standing leg for 1 second.

exercises.name: Leg swings — front/back
exercises.cue: Hold something for balance; relaxed, full range.

exercises.name: Leg swings — side/side
exercises.cue: Open the hip, don't twist the spine.

exercises.name: Walking lunges
exercises.cue: Front knee tracks over second toe; keep torso tall.

exercises.name: Glute bridges
exercises.cue: Squeeze glutes at the top; ribs down.

exercises.name: High knees
exercises.cue: Quick turnover; emphasize lift, not speed.

exercises.name: Strides (quality days only)
exercises.cue: Build to ~85% of 5K pace over 20 sec. 60 sec full recovery between. Skip on easy days.

pre_run.notes: Do this BEFORE every run. On easy/shakeout days, omit strides. On quality days (hill intervals, race-rhythm sessions), include the 3 x strides. During recovery weeks 1-2, do the mobility items only, gently.

exercises.name: Walking cooldown
exercises.cue: Walk until HR is below 110 bpm before stretching.

exercises.name: Standing quad stretch
exercises.cue: Tuck pelvis under to feel the stretch in the front of the hip too.

exercises.name: Standing calf stretch (bent + straight knee)
exercises.cue: Two angles per side: knee straight (gastroc) and knee bent (soleus).

exercises.name: Half-kneeling hip flexor stretch
exercises.cue: Squeeze the back glute first, THEN lean forward.

exercises.name: Pigeon stretch
exercises.cue: Square hips. If knee complains, lie back instead (figure-4 supine).

exercises.name: Foam roll quads, IT band, calves (optional)
exercises.cue: 60 seconds per area; pause and breathe on tender spots.

post_run.notes: Do within 15 minutes of finishing the run. Especially important after long runs and power-climb days — eccentric load + walking cooldown protects the quads.

weekly_targets.notes: Recovery week 1 of 2. Walking only until Friday; first jog steps are symptom-gated. Mileage figure counts jogged minutes only. SYMPTOM GATE all week: any sharp or localized pain in the right lateral ankle, left outer knee, or right forefoot ends the session and pushes the progression back 2 days.
weekly_targets.derivation_rule: DERIVED FIELD — regenerated from this week's session sums (race excluded). Never hand-author. Loaders should assert mileage_mi and vertical_ft equal the session sums within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. W1 EXCEPTION: Week 1 sessions are duration-prescribed walk/jog with no distance or vertical values, so the derived header is 0 by construction. Actual content is ~175 min of walking with ~14 min of jogged intervals. The pre-rev-1.2 header of "3 mi" was a hand-authored estimate of jogged minutes and has been removed rather than fabricated back. LOADER CONVENTION: a session omitting elevation_gain_ft or distance_mi is treated as 0; as of rev 1.3 all such fields are written explicitly, so an absent field now indicates a malformed record rather than a zero.

weeks.week_notes: Days 2-8 post-White River. The job this week is circulation and tissue protection, not fitness. Elevation and gentle walking early; short jog intervals only from Friday, only if walking is fully comfortable. No NSAIDs around any loading (blunts collagen remodeling). Strength plan carries the P1 tendon-entry work (isometrics, no HSR).

days.day_notes: Full rest. Short walks around the house, elevation when sitting, pre-stand mobility. Day 2 post-race.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Flat, supportive shoes, conversational stroll. This is circulation, not training.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Walk only. Note how the right lateral ankle and left knee feel at the start vs. end — this is baseline data for the week.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Slightly longer. Still flat. Stop early without guilt if anything localizes.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Tendon-entry strength session this evening (see strength plan) — isometrics only.

days.day_notes: Rest from walking volume. Daily routines + evening isometrics only. Assess: is walking symptom-free? That answer gates Friday.

sessions.title: Walk + first jog steps (gated)
sessions.key_cue: 6 x 1 min VERY easy jog inside a 45-min walk — ONLY if walking has been fully symptom-free since Wednesday.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Day 6 post-race. If any of the three sites (right lateral ankle, left outer knee, right forefoot) speaks up on the jog steps, drop back to walking and retry Sunday.

days.day_notes: Rest or optional 25-30 min flat walk. Flex day — listen to the legs.

sessions.title: Long walk + jog intervals
sessions.key_cue: 8 x 1 min easy jog inside a 60-min walk if Friday was clean. Gentle terrain OK, nothing steep or technical.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. End-of-week checkpoint: report symptom status — it sets Week 2's walk/run ratios.

weekly_targets.notes: Recovery week 2 of 2. Walk/run progressing toward continuous easy running by Saturday. Still no HSR in the gym, still flat/gentle terrain, still symptom-gated. Target ~12 mi combined walk+run.
weekly_targets.derivation_rule: DERIVED FIELD — regenerated from this week's session sums (race excluded). Never hand-author. Loaders should assert mileage_mi and vertical_ft equal the session sums within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. LOADER CONVENTION: a session omitting elevation_gain_ft or distance_mi is treated as 0; as of rev 1.3 all such fields are written explicitly, so an absent field now indicates a malformed record rather than a zero.

weeks.week_notes: Rebuild week. The pre-race walk/run protocol proved this pathway works — same structure, faster timeline because there is no acute injury, only post-race tissue caution. By Sunday the goal is ~70 min mostly-running. Any regression at the three sites resets to Week 1 Friday level and flags a message to the coach. DECISION POINT AT WEEK'S END (rev 1.3): the W2->W3 step is pre-approved at full size ONLY if Weeks 1 and 2 clear all three symptom gates with no flags. Review the two weeks on Sunday 8/9 before Week 3 starts. Clean = Week 3 runs exactly as written, no further approval needed. Any flag = the pre-approval is void, the ladder re-solves downward, and the 9/13 rehearsal reverts to its 2,600 ft profile. This is the last open human item in the package; everything else is verified and accepted.

days.day_notes: Rest. Daily routines + evening isometrics.

sessions.title: Walk/run 2:2
sessions.key_cue: 2 min easy run / 2 min walk x 10. Flat. Cadence relaxed, no watch-chasing.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. First structured run/walk. Tendon-entry lower session this evening.

sessions.title: Recovery walk
sessions.key_cue: Pure walk between run/walk days.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Upper strength this evening if energy is normal.

sessions.title: Walk/run 4:2
sessions.key_cue: 4 min easy run / 2 min walk x 7-8. Gentle rolling OK, avoid sustained descent.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Second tendon-entry lower session this evening. 48h from Tuesday's.

days.day_notes: Rest.

sessions.title: First continuous run
sessions.key_cue: 25 min continuous easy. Flat. Stop at 25 even if it feels great — it should feel great.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. Milestone session: first continuous run post-race.

sessions.title: Rebuild long walk/run
sessions.key_cue: Mostly easy running with a 2-min walk break every 15 min. Rolling non-technical trail or gravel.
sessions.fueling_notes: Bring 1 gel + water; practice taking it at 30 min even on a short effort — keeps the habit warm.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Recovery. End of recovery block. Clean execution here opens the Build phase: hills return Tuesday.

weekly_targets.notes: Build opens. First hill intervals (short, sub-threshold), first descent skill block (gentle, Gate 1 cleared), first strides. 4th strength session added. Ramp guard: nothing this week exceeds 60% of peak-week session sizes. SUNDAY VERTICAL CHECK (rev 1.3): compare actual GPS weekly vertical against this week's derived vertical_ft. Over by more than ~100 ft, next week's ceiling recomputes off the actual sum and the coach is messaged. There is no spare vertical in the ladder.
weekly_targets.derivation_rule: DERIVED FIELD — regenerated from this week's session sums (race excluded). Never hand-author. Loaders should assert mileage_mi and vertical_ft equal the session sums within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. LOADER CONVENTION: a session omitting elevation_gain_ft or distance_mi is treated as 0; as of rev 1.3 all such fields are written explicitly, so an absent field now indicates a malformed record rather than a zero.

weeks.week_notes: The 9-week shape starts here: Tue hill intervals + PM Lower A (hill strength), Wed easy + upper, Thu easy with descent block + PM Lower B (tendon HSR begins), Fri easy + strides, Sat shakeout/rest + upper, Sun rolling long. INTENSITY MODEL for the block: hill intervals are Z3-capped (the validated HR-led model); short uphill strides (15-20 s) are the only faster work — alactic, low-eccentric, aimed at the +4..8% gait-collapse finding. Strides are pulled first if the lateral ankle objects. ENTRY CONDITION (rev 1.3): this week is conditional on Weeks 1-2 clearing all three symptom gates with no flags. It is the largest single step in the block (+9.5 mi / +2,150 ft on session sums) and is exempt from the ramp guard by settled rule — which means the symptom gates, not arithmetic, are what protect it. If the gates were not clean, do not start this week as written.

days.day_notes: Rest. Post-long-run recovery slot for the rest of the plan.

sessions.title: Hill intervals — intro
sessions.key_cue: 6 x 90 s RUNNING at +5..8% grade, HR under 155, walk-down recovery. PASS CRITERION: run_pct >= 80% on every rep — running cadence sits at 168-176 spm when genuinely run. A rep at 130-140 spm is half-walked and does not count.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Quality. P2 opens. TEST ZONE, not a known deficit: +5..8% is exactly the band where the run-vs-hike question is open (Findings Register F-08). Reps are short on purpose. No poles. TERRAIN: trail, but NON-TECHNICAL — smooth trail, dirt or gravel road all qualify. Uphill running is low-eccentric so the climb itself is tendon-friendly, but technical footing is exactly what provokes the right lateral ankle. Simple footing, consistent pitch. CADENCE CRITERION CORRECTED rev 1.4: the previous 'cadence over 130' target was inherited from walk-contaminated band averages (F-02, retracted). Pass on run share, report cadence_moving_spm.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM hills + PM Lower A (hill strength). Run first.

sessions.title: Easy Z2
sessions.key_cue: Conversational. Nose-breathing test on the flats.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy. Upper A this evening. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard on the nominated denominator. Easy-day volume only; the session's purpose is unchanged.

sessions.title: Easy + descent skill block
sessions.key_cue: Within an easy run: 2 x 0.5 mi at -3..5%, RELAXED running, median running cadence 175+, quiet feet. Non-technical surface.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy + skill. P3 opens gently — Gate 1 is cleared, so moderate-grade descent running begins as the tendon-rebuild medium itself. This is form practice, not load. Lower B (tendon HSR) this evening.

days.day_notes: DOUBLE DAY — AM easy/descent + PM Lower B. Run first.

sessions.title: Easy + first hill strides
sessions.key_cue: 4 x 15 s uphill strides at the end — smooth build to fast-but-relaxed, walk back down. Full recovery.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Easy + strides. Strides gate: only if the week has been symptom-free at the ankle. RATIONALE RE-DERIVED rev 1.4: the original justification cited the +4..8% cadence-collapse finding, which is retracted (F-02) — running cadence is 166-178 spm at every grade. Strides are retained on independent grounds: running economy, and the SSC/elastic-tendon demand of Vermont's 20-28 short climb-descent transitions. Neuromuscular, not cardio — HR is irrelevant on a 15-s rep. TRIM (rev 1.2, Answer A2): volume reduced to bring the week's session sum inside the ramp guard.

days.day_notes: Rest (or optional 20 min shakeout). Upper B this evening — upper is fine the day before a long run.

sessions.title: Rolling long run
sessions.key_cue: Rolling runnable terrain, ~100 ft/mi. RUN everything up to ~8% — walking is a choice, not a default. Hike only the genuinely steep. GAIT RULE: on any climb where you do switch to hiking, hold the hike for >= 60 CONTINUOUS SECONDS rather than oscillating. Gait oscillation is what hid a usable hiking comparator inside the race file for two weeks — 60-second minimum blocks make those seconds analysable at no cost on the day.
sessions.fueling_notes: Race-cadence habit: gel every 30 min, SaltStick at 45 min, ~500 ml/hr.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Long Z2. Vermont-shaped from day one: gravel/dirt rolling routes, NOT the technical-descent mountain routes that produced the June injury. Load-pattern guard is active for the whole block: no technical 20+ milers, minimum 6 days between long runs, terrain rotated. ANALYSIS NOTE (rev 1.5): the >=60 s gait rule exists because PC-1 block construction requires contiguous gait; sub-60 s alternation is unanalysable no matter how much of it there is.

weekly_targets.notes: Volume +~25% on a clean Week 3. Hill reps lengthen to 3 min. Descent blocks grow. Gear-change pickups start Friday (the +2..4% running economy work). SUNDAY VERTICAL CHECK (rev 1.3): compare actual GPS weekly vertical against this week's derived vertical_ft. Over by more than ~100 ft, next week's ceiling recomputes off the actual sum and the coach is messaged. There is no spare vertical in the ladder.
weekly_targets.derivation_rule: DERIVED FIELD — regenerated from this week's session sums (race excluded). Never hand-author. Loaders should assert mileage_mi and vertical_ft equal the session sums within +/-0.5 mi / +/-50 ft and flag on failure. LOADER CONVENTION: a session omitting elevation_gain_ft or distance_mi is treated as 0; as of rev 1.3 all such fields are written explicitly, so an absent field now indicates a malformed record rather than a zero.

weeks.week_notes: Second build week. Everything progresses one notch. Watch the cumulative-fatigue signal on Thursday descents — that is the Vermont-relevant read.

sessions.title: GRADE-ECONOMY TEST (F-08) + reduced hill reps
sessions.key_cue: ROAD CLIMB (Garmin course 499037395, scouted). CONTINUOUS LAPPING — press lap at EVERY transition so work and recovery alternate with no un-lapped time. Auto-lap OFF. L1 flat reference 6 min steady running on the 1% terrain. L2 block A climb 0.00-0.50 @ +5.0%. L3 recovery, walk 0.25 down and 0.25 back up, settle 60-90 s at the 0.50 mark before pressing. L4 block B climb 0.50-1.00 @ +8.5%. L5 recovery, walk down to base. L6 block C repeat 0.00-0.50 @ +5.0%. L7 walk down. L8 4 x 20 s strides. RUN EVERY BLOCK TO COMPLETION at steady running effort — do NOT pace to a cap and do not walk. 157 is an ABORT tripwire, not a target. WALK the recoveries, do not jog them — a jogged recovery lets PC-1 merge block-recovery-block into one running stream with grade floating; walking segments the blocks for free. This changes the parse, not only the load.
sessions.notes: Intensity: Quality / MEASUREMENT. This is the Addendum C s9 test and it is the highest-value measurement in the block (Findings Register F-08). THE QUESTION: running continuously at grade, does HR plateau below the ceiling or rise monotonically until you are forced to walk? Plateau -> P2 becomes volume and execution rehearsal. Monotonic rise -> P2 becomes economy work and Lever C (the ceiling itself) moves to the front. TERRAIN FIELD CORRECTED rev 1.4a: was 'trail', which contradicted the cue. Rolling trail cannot produce a stable continuous grade — grade SD within running blocks averages 4.1 percentage points, which is what defeated the v7 iso-HR rule in the first place. This session REQUIRES a road or graded fireroad climb. PROTOCOL NOTE: turn OFF auto-lap so manual lap presses are the only block boundaries (Parser spec PC-2). READ-OUT REQUIRED: HR start/end/max and slope in bpm/min within each block, pace, cadence_moving_spm, run_pct, and %% of seconds above cap — not block averages. HEAT GATE (convention C-2): coolest available window. Heat index above 85 F invalidates the HR read entirely — if the forecast breaches it, the session SLIPS TO W5 TUESDAY 8/25 and the hill reps run as originally written. The test must precede the 8/27 Gate 2 and 8/30 calibration package. P1 INTERACTION: uphill running is concentric-dominant and race climbing was pain-free, so this is tendon-compatible; confirm the three symptom sites are clear before starting. VERTICAL-NEUTRAL: 800 ft total is UNCHANGED from rev 1.3 — the test blocks are funded by reducing approach and recovery climbing, not by adding gain. W4 sits exactly at the +500 ft ramp cap and has no headroom. COURSE LOCKED rev 1.4b: Garmin course 499037395, road. Measured profile — 1.245 mi, 422 ft, continuous ascent. Block A mi 0.00-0.50 mean +5.0%, grade SD 1.3 pts. Block B mi 0.50-1.00 mean +8.5%, grade SD 0.9 pts. Separation 3.5 percentage points. CUT AT 0.50 (rev 1.4c), replacing an earlier 0.55 offset — same grade quality, cleaner boundary, and 19 ft cheaper on the approach re-climb. REJECTED ALTERNATIVE: 'rest of ascent' mi 0.50-1.245 averages +7.3%, closer to the original +6..7% target, but grade SD doubles to 2.3 pts because the road crests — per-0.1-mi it runs 8.4, 8.3, 8.9, 9.4, 7.5, 7.6, 3.5, 2.8. That average is a steep-plus-flat blend, the same class of artifact as a walk-contaminated band mean. A block whose grade shifts six points partway cannot answer a stable-grade HR question. Trail comparison SD is 4.1 pts, so this road delivers the grade stability the test requires. DESIGN NOTE: the two blocks BRACKET the +5..8% test zone rather than sampling inside it. Both plateau -> the whole zone is runnable. A plateaus and B does not -> the boundary sits inside the zone, interpolate. Neither plateaus -> the boundary is below +5% and P2 reshapes substantially. A pass at +5.0% generalises downward to +3..4%, so the gentle end is covered. Block B at +8.6% is above the rev 1.4 hike line; 'could not run it' is a valid and informative result there. SECOND GENTLE BLOCK RESTORED (rev 1.4d). An earlier draft cut it on budget grounds, using a descend-to-base plus jog-up recovery costing 1.00 mi and 133 ft of re-climb. Athlete proposed walking 0.25 down and 0.25 back up instead — same recovery effect at half the distance and ~60 ft less climbing, and walking descent recovers better than jogging. That saving funds block C. Planned total 4.55 mi / 562 ft against 4.5 / 800. BLOCK C VALUE: repeating +5.0% after block B and a mile of descending is a within-session check on whether the same grade costs more under accumulated work — a cheap partial read on the fatigue question Addendum B v4 s11 withdrew, and the closest approximation to race conditions in the session. First thing dropped if the right lateral ankle responds on the walk-downs. DESCENT LOAD: 1.75 mi of descending, all easy-paced recovery rather than descent work, on a day carrying Lower A in the evening. Keep every descent genuinely easy. FLAT REFERENCE: 1% terrain at the base, confirmed available. Use the longest continuous straight or the widest loop — tight loops depress flat pace through braking and acceleration, which would bias BOTH climb comparisons favourably and corrupt the anchor the whole test rests on. If the loop is tight, note it and the flat figure is treated as a floor rather than a value. STILL TO CONFIRM: 0.55 mi of flat ground at the base for the reference block. Route starts at 5 ft elevation. DATA CAVEAT: Garmin course elevation is DEM-derived at ~27 m point spacing; real road may undulate slightly more than the profile shows. DURATION CHANGED rev 1.4e: 50 -> 70 min. THIS IS A LOAD-FIELD CHANGE and the only one in rev 1.4; distance_mi and elevation_gain_ft remain untouched across the whole revision. Driver is 2.0 mi of recovery walking at ~15-20 min/mi, roughly 30-35 min on its own. Work blocks total ~28 min. The ramp guard governs mileage and vertical, not duration, so weekly compliance is unaffected; walking recovery carries near-zero physiological load. Consequences that DO matter: greater heat exposure, which makes the coolest-window instruction and the 85 F gate more binding, and a longer gap needed before Lower A. BLOCKS ARE DISTANCE-DEFINED, NOT TIME-DEFINED (changed from the original 6-min spec): a physical landmark is a more reliable lap boundary than a timer and keeps each block's grade matched to the measured road segment. Expected durations: L1 6:00 time-capped, L2 6:15-7:30, L4 7:15-9:00, L6 6:30-7:45. Longer than 6 min is an improvement — plateau vs monotonic rise reads more clearly over 8 min. If block B turns into a hike partway, STOP the block there, press lap, and note the distance. That is a result, not a failed session. STRIDES moved from hill to flat (logistics — avoids re-climbing); the session already carries 490 ft of climbing so the climbing-specific stimulus is covered. FLAT REFERENCE TARGET: let HR settle at 140-145, ideally ~142, and let pace be the output. Do NOT set a pace target — fixing pace on the flat fixes the wrong variable and biases both climb comparisons. Expect roughly 11:00-11:30/mi. Carry the same perceived effort into block A. Lower A this evening as scheduled, with adequate gap. READ-OUT ADDITION (rev 1.5, Dispositions s3): report the steep block BOTH uncorrected AND decay-corrected. Estimate time decay linearly between the BLOCK A and BLOCK C midpoints (both +5.0%) and interpolate MULTIPLICATIVELY to BLOCK B — the 8/9 session showed decay as a proportional penalty on a common pace scale (16.1-16.7% across three non-climbing grade bins), not an additive grade term. STATE that the A->C slope contains any fatigue BLOCK B itself induced, so the correction is an UPPER BOUND on decay and the corrected figures are optimistic. The read must hold across BOTH bounds or the session did not settle it. DECLARED ASSUMPTION: the 8/9 climbing bin (+3..+6%) ran 19.8% against 16.1-16.7% for the three non-climbing bins — about 3 points clear on 166 late seconds. If decay RATE differs between +5.0% and +8.5%, the multiplicative interpolation to BLOCK B carries an additional unquantified error. Small sample, stated as an assumption rather than discovered in the read-out. BLOCK NAMING RECONCILED rev 1.5: the disposition was written against the retired 4-block design (BLOCK 2/4 at +3..4%, BLOCK 3 at +6..7%); it maps onto the locked course as A/C and B respectively. Method unchanged.

Detailed stage/pacing plan comes from the Race Strategy project (~2 weeks out) and supersedes the generic caps here. 32-33 mi, ~5,600 ft as 20+ short climbs/descents, 37% gravel road, no poles. HR band note: the race is not a Z2-only event — White River executed as low/mid-Z2 average with designed Z3 excursions; 158 is the never-cross ceiling, exactly the top of Z3 under the corrected table.
